subtopics.title: Selling on Credit — the Invoice and the Debtors Journal

questions.question: The source document that creates a debt when goods are sold on credit is:
options: The receipt
The numbered invoice, issued in duplicate
The credit note
The cash register roll

questions.question: The Debtors Journal records:
options: All sales, cash and credit together
Payments received from debtors
Credit sales of trading stock, and nothing else
Goods returned by debtors

questions.question: Every credit sale must reach two destinations, namely:
options: The Bank account and the Sales account
The CRJ and the CPJ
The trial balance and the statement
The debtor's personal account daily, and the general ledger totals monthly

subtopics.title: Recording and Posting the Debtors Journal

questions.question: Invoice 81 to M. Sithole: goods R2 400 at a 50 percent mark-up on cost. The Cost of Sales entry is:
options: R1 600 — R2 400 divided by 1,5
R1 200 — half of R2 400

questions.question: At month end, the DJ Sales total of R5 100 posts as:
options: Debit Sales, credit Debtors Control
Debit Debtors Control, credit Sales
Debit Bank, credit Sales
Debit Sales, credit Trading Stock

questions.question: The month's DJ posting balances with debits of R8 500 made up of:
options: Sales 5 100 and Trading Stock 3 400
Debtors Control 5 100 and Trading Stock 3 400
Bank 5 100 and Cost of Sales 3 400
Debtors Control 5 100 and Cost of Sales 3 400

questions.question: The timing rule for posting debtors is:
options: Personal accounts daily; control and general ledger totals monthly
Everything monthly
Everything daily
Control daily; personal accounts yearly

questions.question: The document that reduces a debtor's debt is the:
options: Duplicate invoice
Numbered credit note
Debit note
Monthly statement

questions.question: M. Sithole returns undamaged goods invoiced at R600 (cost R400). The DAJ line shows:
options: Debtors Allowances R600 with an empty cost column
Debtors Allowances R400 and Cost of Sales R600
Debtors Allowances R600 and Cost of Sales R400
Only a Cost of Sales entry of R400

questions.question: P. Govender keeps the scratched item and receives R200 off. The cost column stays empty because:
options: No goods moved — only the price adjusted
The cost is too small to record
Allowances never touch the personal accounts
The goods were damaged

questions.question: Returns and allowances go to a separate Debtors Allowances account instead of Sales because:
options: Sales may never be debited under any circumstances
The trial balance requires it
Credit notes are not source documents
Management needs gross sales AND the amount coming back as two visible figures

subtopics.title: The Debtors Ledger at Month End

questions.question: M. Sithole's personal account shows debits of 2 400 and 900 and a credit of 600. His balance is:
options: R2 700 debit
R3 300 debit
R2 700 credit
R3 900 debit

questions.question: The list of debtors totals R4 300. Debtors Control shows debits 5 100 and credits 800. This means:
options: An error exists, since 5 100 less 800 is not 4 300
The list and control agree at R4 300, as they must
The control account must be rebuilt
R800 of debts must be written off

questions.question: Which measure belongs to sound control over credit sales?
options: Granting unlimited credit to loyal customers
Sending statements only when a debtor complains
A credit limit per debtor, monthly statements, and chasing debts the moment terms are exceeded
Letting the debtors clerk receive all payments

questions.question: In the picture, the page-per-person exercise book is:
options: The Debtors Ledger — one personal account per customer
The general journal
The Cash Receipts Journal
The trial balance

questions.question: Debtors Control is described as 'the whole street on one line' because it:
options: Lists each debtor by address
Summarises all debtors as one general ledger balance
Records only the largest debtor
Replaces the personal accounts

questions.question: The 'beautiful lock' between the pages and the street-line is:
options: Each page must be signed by the customer
The street-line is always larger than the pages
Pages are destroyed once control is posted
The sum of all personal balances must equal the control balance

subtopics.title: The Week Mr Sithole Changed His Mind

questions.question: The returned R600 shirt (cost R400) requires:
options: Crediting his page R600, and returning R400 to Trading Stock out of Cost of Sales
Crediting his page R400 only
Debiting his page R600
A price adjustment with no stock entry

questions.question: The scratched kettle Mrs Govender keeps requires:
options: A credit of R200 to her page and R200 back into Trading Stock
Her page credited R200 — and the shelf untouched, since no goods moved
A new invoice for R200
Cost of Sales debited R200

questions.question: The rule that decides whether the cost column writes is:
options: Follow the money — cash entries always write cost
Cost writes only for amounts above R500
Follow the goods — goods back means cost comes back; goods stay means price moves alone
The cost column writes for allowances only

questions.question: A credit limit per debtor exists because:
options: It caps the trust each name carries, so the store can keep saying yes safely
The law sets a maximum of R3 500
It punishes unreliable customers
Statements cannot list more than one page

questions.question: Monthly statements do two quiet jobs, namely:
options: Advertising and stocktaking
Reminding politely and surfacing disputes early
Raising prices and closing accounts
Replacing invoices and credit notes

questions.question: The person who writes the debtors' pages should not receive their payments because:
options: One person cannot work that fast
Debtors prefer paying the owner
Payments are only accepted in cash
Division of duties ensures every rand that moves leaves a paper trail between two sets of hands
